What CTET Paper 2 asks on Playing with Numbers

Questions focus on factors and multiples, prime and composite numbers, divisibility rules, prime factorisation, and finding HCF and LCM. Divisibility and HCF/LCM word problems are the most common.

Key facts & formulas to remember

  • 1 is a factor of every number and is neither prime nor composite; 2 is the only even prime.
  • Divisibility: by 3 if the digit sum is divisible by 3; by 9 if the digit sum is divisible by 9.
  • By 11 if the difference of alternate digit sums is 0 or a multiple of 11.
  • HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
  • Co-prime numbers have HCF = 1 (e.g. 8 and 15).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Calling 1 a prime number.
  • Mixing up HCF (greatest common factor) with LCM (least common multiple).
  • Forgetting that a number is a multiple of itself and of 1.

quiz.title: CTET Playing with Numbers Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper II–pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: CTET Paper 2 Maths: Playing with Numbers

questions.q: If the 6-digit number 452x30 is divisible by 9, what is the value of the digit x?
questions.explanation: By the divisibility rule for 9, the sum of the digits must be divisible by 9. Sum of digits = 4 + 5 + 2 + x + 3 + 0 = 14 + x. The smallest multiple of 9 greater than or equal to 14 is 18, so 14 + x = 18, giving x = 4.

questions.q: A number is divisible by both 5 and 12. By which of the following numbers must it always be divisible?
questions.explanation: If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers, it is also divisible by their product. Since HCF(5, 12) = 1, the two numbers are co-prime, so the number must be divisible by 5 x 12 = 60.

questions.q: In the prime factorization of 180, what is the exponent of 3?
questions.explanation: Prime factorization of 180 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 = 2^2 x 3^2 x 5^1. The exponent of 3 is 2.

questions.q: The HCF of two co-prime numbers is always equal to:
questions.explanation: By definition, two numbers are co-prime if they have no common factor other than 1. Hence their Highest Common Factor is always 1.

questions.q: In a 3 x 3 magic square, if the magic sum (sum of numbers in each row, column, and diagonal) is 45, what is the value of the central number?
questions.explanation: In any 3 x 3 magic square, the magic sum equals 3 times the central entry. So the central number = 45 / 3 = 15.

questions.q: If the 7-digit number 732k814 is divisible by 11, what is the value of digit k?
questions.explanation: Number the digits from the right: positions 1,3,5,7 hold 4,8,2,7 (sum 21); positions 2,4,6 hold 1,k,3 (sum 4+k). For divisibility by 11 the difference 21-(4+k)=17-k must be a multiple of 11. Taking 17-k=11 gives k=6, which is the only valid single digit.

questions.q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 288 respectively. If one of the numbers is 72, find the other number.
questions.explanation: HCF x LCM equals the product of the two numbers, so 12 x 288 = 72 x (other number). The other number = (12 x 288) / 72 = 48. Check: 48 x 72 = 3456 = 12 x 288.

questions.q: Four bells toll together at 9:00 AM. They toll at intervals of 6, 8, 12, and 18 minutes respectively. At what time will they toll together next?
questions.explanation: The bells toll together again after a time equal to the LCM of 6, 8, 12, and 18 minutes. LCM = 2^3 x 3^2 = 72 minutes = 1 hour 12 minutes. Adding this to 9:00 AM gives 10:12 AM.

questions.q: How many pairs of natural numbers exist such that their sum is 84 and their HCF is 12?
questions.explanation: Let the two numbers be 12a and 12b, where a and b are co-prime. Then 12a + 12b = 84 gives a + b = 7. The pairs of positive integers summing to 7 that are co-prime are (1,6), (2,5), and (3,4) - all three pairs work, giving three number pairs: (12,72), (24,60), and (36,48).

questions.q: What is the smallest digit 'a' such that the 5-digit number 34a28 is divisible by both 3 and 4?
questions.explanation: The last two digits, 28, are divisible by 4 regardless of a, so divisibility by 4 always holds. For divisibility by 3, the digit sum 3+4+a+2+8 = 17+a must be a multiple of 3, which happens for a = 1, 4, or 7. The smallest such digit is 1.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to find HCF and LCM?
faq.a: Use prime factorisation: HCF is the product of common prime factors at their lowest powers; LCM uses all prime factors at their highest powers. For two numbers you can also use HCF × LCM = product of the numbers.

faq.q: Which divisibility rules are most tested?
faq.a: Rules for 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 11 appear most often. The rule for 11 (alternating digit-sum difference) is the one candidates forget.
